newsitem.title: JAPAN: Trading firms taking advantage of Japan premium.
newsitem.headline: Trading firms taking advantage of Japan premium.

text.p: Some of Japan's big trade houses are taking advantage of the "Japan premium" -- the extra cost Japanese banks must pay to raise funds in the eurodollar interbank market -- by lending dollar funds to the banks through overseas financial units, bankers said on Wednesday.

The relatively higher credit ratings enjoyed by the trading companies compared to the banks allow their overseas units to raise dollars below LIBOR and earn interest rate spreads by lending to Japanese banks.

Mitsubishi Corporation Finance Plc, a London-based, wholly-owned financial unit of Mitsubishi Corp, raises funds in the eurodollar market at a cost of about 0.01 percentage point below LIBOR on average, a spokesman for the parent Mitsubishi Corp in Tokyo said.
MCF earns an interest spread of around three basis points by lending to Japanese banks. he said.
Long-term debts of Mitsubishi Corp and MCF are both rated double A minus by Standard & Poor's Corp.
Only two Japanese banks are assigned ratings of double A minus or above by S&P.
Major Japanese banks currently pay around 5.9 percent for three-month eurodollar deposits, about 0.09 percentage point above the prevailing rate.
The premium on three-month eurodollar deposits had widened as much a as 0.22 percentage point in late March due to strong fund demand at the end of Japan's fiscal year.
Japanese banks are charged the premium as non-Japanese institutions remain cautious about lending to them due to worries about Japan's banking system.
